sources.citation: Green, Christopher R. & Katrina Smith. 2024. Poised to pivot: Kenyan Maay's restricted tone system. In C. R. Green & S. Lotven (eds), The Ghanaian Linguistics Nexus (Contemporary African Linguistics 9), ch. 13. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.11091843.
sources.note: Open access; read the LaTeX source. Jiiddu appears once, in the introduction, only as one of the Digil languages (Dabarre, Garre, Jiiddu, Tunni) related to Maay; nothing about Jiiddu stress or tone. Its bibliography cites Lamberti 1986 as the dialect survey.

sources.note: The only dedicated grammar sketch of Jiiddu (Glottolog's ranked source); 98 pp. in German, probably with a Lautlehre/Akzent section. Unpublished; a copy exists in Hammarström's files (africa/) and presumably at the Köln institute.

sources.note: Comparative dialect survey (Lamberti's Köln PhD), the fullest treatment of the Digil lects including Jiiddu, tagged phonology in hh.bib; the most likely place for an explicit statement on Jiiddu accent/tone. HathiTrust holds a search-only copy (uva.x001254520) that a logged-in reader could full-text search for 'Jiiddu' + 'Akzent'/'Ton'.
